criteria.distribution: the four joint classes and the per-slot classes are all reported by count
criteria.mainline: each of the four failures is classified and the number the bridge would fix is counted
criteria.samples: at least three real cases, including one joint no_match and one published failure
criteria.verdict: exactly one of the three names, decided by the frozen rule
criteria.wiring: route equality, name-byte equality, and the question-vs-record coordinate difference are reported with concrete byte offsets

definition.closed_state: the nine closed-state readings stay equal before and after
definition.key_rule: frozen wording rule: the key is the description phrase exactly as it appears in the record (ordered characters, containment read); names never enter the key
definition.mainline_comparison: the four published 19.2v confirm failures are re-read from the report (never re-scored); for each, the gate reports whether the bridge's choice would differ from the route 19.2v took, and whether the failure is already selection-correct
definition.question: can the written bridge serve Task1, or does it live in a parallel world?
definition.questions: Task1's own 192 confirm goals 让{object description}到{place description}。 (12 worlds x 16); no question is authored for this gate

readings.coordinate_check: the bridge's span is a character span in the QUESTION; the copy chain's field is a byte span in the RECORD; the report must state the difference in bytes, not call it agreement
readings.joint: R54' joint rule applied unchanged: every key of the goal must sit in one record; exactly one -> selected, two or more -> ambiguous_multiple_records, zero -> no_match, no key -> no_keys
readings.per_slot: the bridge's own frozen two-pass read, one record per description; answers are checked against the record the fixture says carries that description
readings.wiring: for every answered slot: does the bridge's record index equal the copy chain's route, and does the bridge's value equal the copy chain's own name-field bytes record[start:end] from field_bounds

definition.sealed_set: confirm worlds are materialised once for their record and goal bytes only; zero model forwards, zero scoring, and the published 19.2v reading is not recomputed
definition.source_records: Task1's eight candidate records per world, raw bytes exactly as the frozen generator writes them; no rewriting, no added fields, no new key type
definition.training: zero training, zero optimizer steps, zero Adam, zero parameters

verdict_rule.bridge_parallel_world: per-slot address exact below 0.5: the bridge cannot even name the records
verdict_rule.bridge_partial_overlap: otherwise; the report must name the overlapping part and the part that does not
verdict_rule.bridge_reaches_mainline: joint selects one record for all 192 goals AND per-slot exact 384/384 AND wiring exact 384/384 AND the bridge fixes at least one of the four failures

mainline_relation.how: the bridge is built from Task1's own eight record lines and asked Task1's own 192 confirm goals; its routes and names are compared against the fixture's records and against the published 19.2v failure rows
mainline_relation.limit: this gate cannot change 188/192 by itself: it only decides whether wiring the bridge in could change it, and the answer is read from the four failures
mainline_relation.not_a_proxy: no fixture-world data is used for the judgement; every record and goal is Task1's
mainline_relation.which_reading: Task1's record choice (route) and copied name per goal, and whether the bridge repairs any of the four published confirm failures

joint.why: every Task1 record carries exactly one description, so no single record can contain both keys of a goal; the joint rule can only return no_match

mainline.why: all four published failures are extra_bytes at answer position 27 with both spans aligned: the stop edge, not the record choice

per_slot.why: each description occurs in exactly one record, so the two-pass read is unique

wiring.why: the bridge's value is the same name field the copy chain derives from the record

sealed_set_note: confirm materialisation registered in D-20261109-57: record and goal bytes only, zero model forwards, zero scoring
